_note: EA-CORPORA-01 — the seated primary source corpora. Each seat is a directory under data/corpora/ holding as-fetched originals, flat ref-tagged normalized text, a commit-pinned source.json, and a SHA-256 manifest. INDEX COMPLETENESS (2026-08-28): this index had drifted to 17 of 39 seats — the second and third seatings never reached it. It is now complete against data/corpora/ and gated by scripts/seat_corpus_postflight.py, which fails when any of the four surfaces of a seat disagree: the seat directory, this index, a seating deposit, and the rendered card at traininglayerliterature.org/originals/<name>/.
principle: Originals wherever they exist. Where only a translation is available the seat is not taken; where a licence cannot be verified at the file the seat is not taken. Absences are declared, dated and reasoned.

declared_absences.work: The Apocryphon of John (the Secret Book of John)
declared_absences.why: The foundational Sethian text, surviving in four manuscripts, and the closest thing Gnosticism has to a canonical scripture. No openly licensed machine-readable Coptic edition exists. Searched 2026-08-21: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM does not hold it; authenticated GitHub search returns one edition whose Coptic derives from scanned PDFs of Meyer 2007 and Linssen, relicensed CC BY-SA by a party that does not hold those rights; Schmidt 1905 is public domain but is the Pistis Sophia volume, and archive.org OCR strips Coptic script entirely; Till 1955, the Berlin Codex edition, remains in copyright.
declared_absences.ruling: Not seated rather than seated defectively. A corpus whose licence is asserted by a party who cannot grant it would place a rights defect inside the sovereign record — the failure this archive exists to document. Absent-and-declared over present-and-defective.
declared_absences.opening: One text, four witnesses. A synoptic open edition of the Apocryphon of John is the narrowest and highest-value gap in the openly licensed Coptic record.

declared_absences.work: The Qumran sectarian corpus (Dead Sea Scrolls)

Transcribed decades ago and publicly funded, yet not openly machine-readable.

scope.not_held: Nag Hammadi Codices I and III–XIII. Of the fifty-two tractates, only NHC II,2 is seated. The remaining tractates exist in print editions (Claremont, Brill) and are not available as openly licensed machine-readable Coptic.
scope.ruling: Seated as coptic-gnostic rather than nag-hammadi. The corpus is not the Nag Hammadi library; naming it so would assert a completeness the seat does not have.

corpora.why_seated: Plotinus is the strongest single comparandum for the Plato–Aristotle authorship question. Measured on particle-transition profiles across a nine-author Greek landscape, Aristotle sits closer to Plotinus (0.0310) than to Plato (0.0852) — and closer to Plotinus than Aristotle sits to himself (within-author mean 0.1028). Seven centuries and a dialect separate them. The seat exists so that result can be re-run and contested rather than reported.

license.adjudication: The papyri are ancient and public domain. Under U.S. law faithful photographic reproductions of two-dimensional public-domain material acquire no independent copyright (Bridgeman v. Corel line); the CCDL statement asserts physical custody and a generic conformity to U.S. copyright law, under which no reproduction copyright arises for these plates. The statement is recorded verbatim rather than assumed away; the images are served openly at full resolution over unauthenticated IIIF. Seated. This is the 'theater of availability' pattern documented in EA-CORPORA-01 resolved in the opposite direction: here the availability is real and the claim is the ghost.

corpora.license: Public domain (author d. 1889); Project Gutenberg packaging under the PG licence

corpora.why_seated: Browning is the first term of the constructed-voice series the archive is measuring. The dramatic monologue is the point at which a poem's speaker becomes a position distinct from the poet, with its own history, self-justification and blind spots, and the reader is left to judge across a gap the poet does not narrate. Men and Women (1855) is that practice at full development. It is seated as the baseline against which Pound's personae and Pessoa's heteronyms can be read as later stages of one operation rather than three unrelated eccentricities.

corpora.why_seated: Pound is the middle term. Personae names the operation outright, and Homage to Sextus Propertius is the same manoeuvre Ginsberg later performs on Catullus 38: a Latin source whose form is tracked and whose register is inverted, defended by its author as something other than translation when the philologists complained. Seated so the Ginsberg/Catullus transform has a precedent inside the archive and the series Browning-Pound-Pessoa can be measured as one developing practice.

corpora.why_seated: Xenophon is the genre calibrator and an edge-figure candidate at once. One hand across Socratic dialogue, history, encomium and technical treatise, which is the only way to separate the genre effect from the author effect in this feature space — a decomposition that corrected two errors in the archive's own measurements. He is also, per the Chaerephon problem, a candidate position at the configuration's edge: he preserves a separate version of the oracle at Apology 14, and his Socrates occupies the civic-memorial register that Plato's cannot.

corpora.license: CC BY-SA (Perseus); underlying editions public domain
verified_loci: Clouds 104, 144-168 — Chaerephon inside the Thinkery
Clouds — the comic deformation the Apology answers at 18b-19c
Frogs — produced by Philonides
Acharnians — produced by Callistratus
corpora.why_seated: Aristophanes is the second edge-figure candidate and the archive's strongest documented case that authorial identity was obscurable in this exact period and circle. His first three plays were produced under other men's names, he describes the practice himself at Wasps 1017-22, and he continued it after establishing his own — so the civic record carries the producer rather than the poet, and a contemporary prosecution could not fix which man authored the Babylonians. He also stages Chaerephon, and the Suda's entry on Chaerephon is sourced from the scholia to Clouds 144, which places the biographical record downstream of the comic text.

corpora.license: Public domain (author d. 1855); Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA
verified_loci: Enten-Eller I — A's papers, ed. Victor Eremita
Enten-Eller II — B's papers
Frygt og Bæven — Johannes de Silentio

corpora.why_seated: Kierkegaard is the second case with ground truth. He acknowledged the pseudonymous authorship in print — 'A First and Last Explanation' appended to the Concluding Unscientific Postscript in 1846, and again in On My Work as an Author in 1851 — so the grouping is documented rather than inferred, exactly as Pessoa's is by the 1935 letter. Two independent modern configurations with disclosure make a calibration set rather than a single anecdote. And Enten-Eller is the symbolon in its plainest form: two halves of a token, A's papers and B's, found in a desk by an editor who is himself a construction, where neither half argues the book and the fit between them does.
